summary: Adds project review publish, the last bookkeeping step of a review. It takes a body file and an optional JSON list of findings, writes the signature line and marker itself from the review's state and one clock reading, checks every finding's anchor against the pull request's diff hunks, runs the collision check against the loop's record, and submits one review.

After it submits, it runs the ending #127's plan review settled on, in this order: draft transition (self-review only), re-read of the review and draft, appending to the loop's record, deleting the start comment, and releasing the lock. It records the submission before any of those steps, so a failed run exits non-zero and a retry finishes the same review instead of posting a second one.
review-changes and start-review-loop now call the command instead of carrying gh snippets, and the loop keeps a loop id instead of its own record.

cards.title: What publish does, in order
cards.html:
1. Refuse on a closed PR, a moved head, a collision, a bad anchor, a bad body, or a verdict that disagrees with the census; each refusal exits 1 and keeps the lock
  2. POST one review: COMMENT (self), REQUEST_CHANGES, COMMENT, or APPROVE under review.allow_approve (cross-author)
  3. Write published to the state file
  4. gh pr ready / --undo on a self-review only
  5. Re-read the review body and draft
  6. Append the id to loops/<id>/published.json
  7. Delete the start comment, then release the lock

groups.title: The publish command
groups.kicker: review.py's new Publishing section and its CLI wiring
intro: compose builds the signature and marker and fills the body's placeholders only in prose. CODE masks fenced blocks and inline spans, PLACEHOLDER matches only the five known names, and OWN_MARKER refuses only a line-start <!-- projector-review|finding comment. check_threads validates each finding against diff_lines, which reads every page of pulls/<n>/files. check_collision reads the per-loop record, and publish runs the ordered ending.
The CLI reads review.allow_approve from the checkout recorded in the state file, so the setting is per repository.
concepts: Every SHA comes from the state file or GitHub, never an argument.
A published entry with a live start comment marks a submitted but unfinished publish, and a retry takes the finishing branch.

checks.text: The draft transition runs only when self_review is true, so a cross-author pull request's draft state is never touched.
The lock is unlinked only after the start comment is deleted and the state is written, and every ReviewError before that leaves it in place.
reviewer_verdicts and diff_lines both use --paginate, so the 30-row reviews page can't hide a verdict.
Text outside a code span is filled, text inside one stays verbatim, and a {census} that appears only inside code is refused.

Under a loop, --second-verdict is ignored for another loop's verdict (review.py:611), so if the user answers that this loop continues, publish still can't post on that SHA. The plan scoped the override to runs outside a loop.
review.py:648: the PLACEHOLDER.search test is implied by the {census} test beside it, and the code is stripped twice (P3).
